text: Gael García Bernal (Spanish: [ɡaˈel ɣaɾˈsi.a βeɾˈnal]; born 30 November 1978) is a Mexican actor and filmmaker known for his roles in films such as Amores perros (2000), Y tu mamá también (2001), Bad Education (2004), The Motorcycle Diaries (2004), Babel (2006), Coco (2017), Old (2021), Cassandro (2023), and Magellan (2025). On television, he played music conductor Rodrigo De Souza in the series Mozart in the Jungle (2014–2018) and starred as the titular character in the Disney+ special Werewolf by Night (2022). He was nominated for a BAFTA Award for Best Actor in a Leading Role in 2005 for his portrayal of young Che Guevara in The Motorcycle Diaries and won his first Golden Globe Award for Best Actor – Television Series Musical or Comedy in 2016 for Mozart in the Jungle. He co-founded the production company Canana Films with fellow actor Diego Luna in Mexico City. In 2016, Time magazine included him in its annual Time 100 list of the most influential people, and in 2020, The New York Times ranked him No. 25 in its list of the 25 Greatest Actors of the 21st Century. Born in Guadalajara, Jalisco, Mexico, he is the son of Patricia Bernal, an actress and former model, and José Ángel García, an actor and director; his stepfather is Sergio Yazbek, whom his mother married when he was young. He began acting at age one and spent much of his teen years in telenovelas. García Bernal and Diego Luna were friends from childhood in Mexico City. At age fourteen, he taught indigenous people in Mexico to read, often working with the Huichol people; at fifteen, he participated in peaceful demonstrations supporting the Zapatista uprising of 1994. He studied philosophy at UNAM but took a sabbatical during a student strike to travel in Europe, later becoming the first Mexican accepted to study at the Central School of Speech and Drama in London and attending the European Graduate School for a master's in media and communication. After gaining success in telenovelas, Mexican director Alejandro González Iñárritu offered him a role in his debut feature, Amores perros (2000), which won critical acclaim and was nominated for an Academy Award for Best Foreign Language Film. His next role was in Alfonso Cuarón's Y tu mamá también (2001), which achieved crossover success in the U.S. and became the second-highest grossing Spanish-language film there. The following year, he portrayed Che Guevara in the 2002 TV miniseries Fidel and Father Amaro in the box-office record-breaking El crimen del Padre Amaro (2002). He reprised Che Guevara in The Motorcycle Diaries (2004), which broke the box office record set by Y tu mamá también three years earlier and earned him a BAFTA nomination in 2005. He also performed in theatre, including a 2005 production of Bodas de Sangre by Federico García Lorca at the Almeida Theatre in London. He has worked with acclaimed directors such as González Iñárritu, Pedro Almodóvar, Walter Salles, Alfonso Cuarón, Michel Gondry, and Iciar Bollaín, and has taken on English-language roles, including in Gondry's The Science of Sleep and The King, which received positive reviews. In 2007, he directed his first feature film, Déficit. He starred in the 2008 film Blindness, an adaptation of José Saramago's Nobel Prize-winning novel, where characters have no names or histories; director Fernando Meirelles noted that García Bernal focused on what his character wanted rather than their past. He again collaborated with Diego Luna in Rudo y Cursi, directed by Carlos Cuarón. The duo owns Canana Films, which recently partnered with Golden Phoenix Productions to produce television documentaries on the unsolved murders of over 300 women in Ciudad Juárez. In May 2010, he made a cameo as himself playing Cristiano Ronaldo in the Nike advertisement Write the Future. In 2010, he co-directed with Marc Siver four short films titled "Los Invisibles" for Amnesty International, focusing on Central American migrants in Mexico, their journey, risks, hopes, and contributions to Mexico, the U.S., and the world; he directed the films, conducted interviews, and narrated them. He starred in Even the Rain (2010), Spain's official entry for the 2011 Academy Awards. He narrated Human Planet for Hispanic audiences, which premiered on Discovery en Español on 25 April 2011 and aired on Discovery Channel in Latin America on 12 May. In 2014, he appeared in the American Spanish-language comedy film Casa de mi padre, opposite Will Ferrell, where he played a feared drug lord, marking his third collaboration with Diego Luna. He was also set to star in film adaptations of José Agustín's Ciudades Desiertas and Jon Stewart's directorial biopic Rosewater, in which he portrayed Maziar Bahari to critical acclaim, and was scheduled to appear in the 20th Century Fox reboot Zorro film Zorro Reborn, with a script by Glen Gers, Lee Shipman, and Brian McGeevy. In April 2014, he joined the main competition jury at the 2014 Cannes Film Festival. In June 2014, he began production on the dramatic comedy Zoom, directed by Pedro Morelli. In 2014, he was cast as Rodrigo de Souza in the Amazon Studios series Mozart in the Jungle, a role that earned him a Golden Globe in 2016. In 2016, he starred in two films submitted for the Academy Award for Best Foreign Language Film: Desierto (Mexico) and Neruda (Chile). In 2017, he was named a member of the U.S. Dramatic Jury at the 2017 Sundance Film Festival and provided the voice of Héctor, a trickster protagonist, in the Pixar film Coco. He founded The Ambulante Documentary Film Festival, which brings documentary films to underserved areas, and helped create the Amnesty International series Los Invisibles; for this work, he received the Washington Office on Latin America's Human Rights Award in 2011. In October 2019, he and Diego Luna joined the Creative Advisory Board for EXILE Content alongside Adam Grant. In 2021, he starred in the M. Night Shyamalan thriller Old. In November 2021, he was cast in the Disney+ special Werewolf by Night by Marvel Studios. In 2024, he starred with Diego Luna in the Hulu original miniseries La Máquina. In 2025, he played Ferdinand Magellan in the historical drama Magellan, directed by Lav Diaz; the film is an international co-production between the Philippines, Spain, Portugal, Taiwan, and France and premiered at the 2025 Cannes Film Festival, being announced as the Philippines' official submission for Best International Feature Film at the 98th Academy Awards. García Bernal met Argentine actress Dolores Fonzi on the set of Private Lives in 2001; their son was born on 8 January 2009 in Madrid, Spain, and their daughter on 4 April 2011 in Buenos Aires, Argentina. He divides his time between Buenos Aires and Mexico City. He has been in a relationship with Mexican journalist Fernanda Aragonés since 2019 and had a child with her on 30 September 2021. He describes himself as "culturally Catholic but spiritually agnostic." He has received awards including the Ariel Award, BAFTA Awards, Cannes Film Festival recognition, Golden Globe Awards, and Goya Awards.
